operative_quotes:
1. Each player takes an action card and all pieces of one player color. Put every scoring chip on **0**. Choose a banker; put money and tiles within reach.
2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.
answers.answer: Each player gets two cards and places markers on those lots, then takes the sum of the two printed money values. Discard those cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces. Remove End of Game while shuffling/dealing; after setup deals, divide the remaining deck into four roughly equal stacks, place End of Game atop stack four, then place the other three stacks above it.

operative_quotes: 5. Each player rolls **2 dice**. The highest roller takes the player card and the first turn. After each turn, pass it to the player on the **left**.
Each normal turn has **Draw**, then **Play**. Trading is also possible at any time, subject to the restrictions below.
answers.answer: Each player rolls two dice; the highest roller takes the first turn. After each turn, pass the player card left. A normal turn consists of Draw followed by Play; trading may occur at any time subject to its restrictions.

clauses: whether printed setup value pays again
operative_quotes:
1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. Apply the dice/marker supply rules if necessary and settle any boss tie before paying casinos.
2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.

3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**.
answers.answer: The empty lot is acquired immediately when drawn, before payouts: place your marker on it. It then pays its owner $1 from the bank in that draw’s payout. Printed card money values apply only during setup, so they do not pay again.

operative_quotes: 1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. Apply the dice/marker supply rules if necessary and settle any boss tie before paying casinos.
4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss.
answers.answer: Replace the opponent’s die with your own at its current value of 5; keep the casino tile in place. After resolving any boss tie, matching-color payout money for that die goes to you, at $1 per pip ($5).

operative_quotes: A **casino** is one tile or an edge-connected group of same-color tiles on the same block. Same-color edge neighbors merge immediately into one casino, even if their dice belong to different players. Diagonal contact alone does not connect them; casinos cannot be subdivided after joining.

The **boss** is the player owning the **highest individual die** in that casino, not the most dice or the highest sum of pips. Several highest dice belonging to the same player are sufficient to make that player boss. Resolve highest ties between different players immediately as described under **Boss ties**.
answers.answer: Same-color tiles on the same block merge as soon as they are edge-connected; diagonal contact does not join them. Once joined, they cannot be subdivided. The boss is determined by the highest individual die, not total dice or total pips.

clauses: money per player from casino dice
operative_quotes: 2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.

4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss. **Points:** only the casino’s boss receives **1 point per tile** in that casino. Follow the scoring-break and separate-casino rules below.
answers.answer: Red receives $5 for Red’s die plus $2 for Red’s two marked lots, totaling $7. Blue receives $3 + $2 = $5 from Blue’s dice. Red is boss with the highest individual die (5), so Red receives 3 points for the three-tile casino; Blue receives 0 points.

clauses: qualification when one tile touches Strip
operative_quotes: 3. **The indicated casinos pay money and points:** a single-color card pays every casino of that color anywhere on the board. A **Pay The Strip** card instead pays every casino with at least **one edge adjacent to The Strip**, regardless of color. A qualifying casino pays for **all its tiles**, not only the tile touching The Strip.
answers.answer: A color card pays every casino of that color anywhere. Pay The Strip pays every casino of any color with at least one edge adjacent to The Strip. If one tile in a casino touches the Strip, the casino qualifies and all its tiles pay.

operative_quotes: On your own turn you may **build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize and gamble** in **any order**, or stop taking actions. You may repeat actions except **gamble is limited to once per turn**, and **no die may be reorganized more than once per turn**. You must be able to pay the stated action cost. After each action check for boss ties and settle them before continuing.
No player may take an action on another player’s turn. Trading itself is not an action.
answers.answer: On your own turn you may build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, and gamble in any order, repeating actions except gamble is limited to once and a die cannot be reorganized twice that turn. Another player may not take an action on your turn.

operative_quotes: Choose **a lot you own**. Take back its marker, choose an **available** casino tile of any color, pay the **price printed on the lot**, and place the tile there. Put one of your dice on it with the **lot’s printed die value** face up. Edge-connected same-color tiles merge immediately; boss control may change.
answers.answer: Pay $6, take back your lot marker, choose any color with an available tile, place it on the lot, and put one of your dice there showing 2.

operative_quotes: You must be **boss of the casino** you expand. Choose an **empty, unowned lot sharing an edge** with it, pay **twice that lot’s printed price**, and place an available tile of the **same color** there. Put your die on it at the **lot’s printed die value**. You cannot sprawl into another player’s marked lot, your own marked lot, a built space or a merely diagonal neighbor. Without an available tile of the required color, you cannot sprawl.
answers.answer: As boss, pay twice $9 = $18; place an available gold tile and a die showing 3. You cannot sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a merely diagonal lot.

operative_quotes:
You must be **boss**. Choose a **new color with enough available tiles for the entire casino**. Pay **$5 per tile** and replace **every tile** of that casino with the new color, returning the old tiles to their supply. Dice stay with their holdings and keep their values. You cannot remodel just part of a casino.

The result merges with any edge-connected casino of the new color. The highest individual die in the resulting casino determines the boss, so a remodel may hand control to another player; settle any cross-player highest tie immediately.
answers.answer: Only the casino’s boss may remodel. For two tiles, choose a new color with at least two available tiles, pay $10, replace both tiles and return the old tiles; dice and values remain. The remodeled casino merges with an edge-connected casino of its new color. If that merged casino’s highest individual die belongs to the neighboring casino’s player and beats yours, that player becomes boss; settle any cross-player tie immediately.

operative_quotes:
You need **at least one die** in the casino; you **need not be boss** and may reorganize a casino containing only your dice.

1. Pay **$1 per pip on every die in that casino**, including opponents’ dice, using their values before the roll.
2. **Reroll all dice**, not a chosen subset. Each player rolls their own dice.
3. Each player puts their rerolled dice back on **their own original tiles**. If they have multiple dice, they choose how to assign the rolled values among those tiles; they cannot move onto another player’s former tile. Temporary markers can help remember the original holdings.
answers.answer: Yes. A non-boss with one die in the casino may reorganize it. That player pays $1 × (5+3+2) = $10, including for opponents’ dice. All three dice reroll; each owner rolls their own dice. Each returns to its owner’s original tile; an owner with multiple dice may choose how to assign the rolled values among that owner’s original tiles.

operative_quotes: You may reorganize different casinos, but **no die can be reorganized twice during the same turn**. A casino containing **any die already reorganized that turn cannot be reorganized**, even after a merger into a larger casino. This limit applies to paid reorganization, **not free boss-tie rerolls**, which happen as often as necessary. Settle boss ties after the action.
answers.answer: No. The larger merged casino contains a die already reorganized this turn, so it cannot be reorganized again. Free boss-tie rerolls are not prohibited by that paid-reorganization limit and may occur as often as necessary.

clauses: cross-player highest tie procedure and cost
boss if tied fives reroll below Green 4
operative_quotes:
If **two or more players** tie for the **highest** value in a casino, reroll **all dice currently tied for highest**, **for free**. Leave smaller dice untouched. Reassess the highest value across the whole casino after each roll. If different players still tie for the current highest, reroll the current highest dice again. Continue until only **one player** owns the highest value; several highest dice belonging to that one player need no reroll.

A tie among smaller dice does nothing. If tied bosses roll below a previously smaller die, that unchanged die’s owner becomes boss. For example, Red 5 and Blue 5 reroll to 3 while Green 4 stays: Green becomes boss, without rerolling the 3s further.
answers.answer: Red’s and Blue’s tied highest 5s reroll for free; Green’s 4 stays. If both reroll to 3, Green’s unchanged 4 is highest and Green becomes boss. If all tied highest dice belong to one player, no reroll is needed. A tie among smaller dice does nothing.

operative_quotes: **Once during your own turn**, choose a casino where **another player is boss**, and give that player the **House card**. If no opponent bosses a casino, you cannot gamble. You may bet no more than **all three limits**: **$5 per tile in that casino**, **your available money**, and **the boss’s available money**.
answers.answer: The limits are $20 (four tiles), your $18, and the boss’s $15, so the maximum bet is $15. Give the House card to the boss. You may gamble once this turn.

clauses: doubled payout limited by $7 boss cash
operative_quotes:
| Dice sum | Result |
|---|---|
| 3, 4, 9, 10 or 11 | You win: the boss pays you **the bet amount**. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 2 or 12 | You win double: the boss pays you **twice the bet**, limited to the money the boss actually has. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 5, 6, 7 or 8 | You lose: pay **the bet amount** to the boss. |

The bank does not cover an unpaid portion of a doubled win in standard play.
answers.answer: For a $4 bet: sums 3, 4, 9, 10, or 11 win $4 from the boss; sums 2 or 12 win double ($8), but with $7 cash the boss pays only $7; sums 5, 6, 7, or 8 lose $4 to the boss. The bank does not cover the unpaid doubled portion. A winning bettor keeps/gets back their stake, so the stake is not also lost.
evidence: Actions — Gamble, results table and standard-play clarification

operative_quotes:
Players may trade **at any time, even off-turn**, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Multiple players may participate. Trade any combination of **money, lots, dice in casinos and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn**.

For a transferred lot replace the owner’s marker with the recipient’s marker. For a transferred casino die replace it with the recipient’s die, retaining the **current pip value**, not the board’s printed die. A die trade can therefore change the boss and cause an immediate highest tie.

You **cannot trade points or casino tiles**, or promise actions, exchanges or transfers for **future turns**. **No player can perform an action on another player’s turn.** A current-turn action can be part of a trade only for the player whose turn it is. If something prevents an element of a trade from happening, the subsequent steps of that trade do not occur.
answers.answer: Trading may happen any time, including off-turn, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Players may trade money, lots, casino dice, and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn. Transfer a lot by replacing its marker; transfer a die by replacing it with the recipient’s die at the current pip value. Points and casino tiles cannot be traded, and actions/exchanges/transfers cannot be promised for future turns. A player cannot perform an action on another player’s turn.

clauses: single award from score 8 for each value
operative_quotes:
For example, from **8**: an award of **1** leaves you on 8; **2 or 3** takes you to **10**; **4 or 5** takes you to **12**.

When several casinos pay you points on one turn, score them **individually, from smallest to largest**, choosing the order of equal-size casinos. You cannot combine their awards to cross a break. Several separate one-tile casinos therefore still cannot move a chip from 8 to 10.
answers.answer: From 8: award 1 leaves you at 8; awards 2 or 3 leave you at 10; awards 4 or 5 leave you at 12. Separate one-tile casinos cannot combine awards to cross a break. Score each casino individually from smallest to largest; choose the order for equal-size casinos.

clauses: End of Game draw and remaining actions/trades
operative_quotes:
As soon as anyone draws **End of Game**, the game ends immediately. Do not take Play actions or initiate trades after that draw. Make the **final payout for all owned lots and all casinos touching The Strip**, using normal money, boss-point and scoring-break rules. Highest score after that payout wins. If tied for most points, the tied player with **most money** wins. The source gives no further tiebreak if both remain equal.

In this base game, a player also **wins immediately at 90+ points**.
answers.answer: Drawing End of Game immediately ends play: take no Play actions and initiate no trades. Pay out all owned lots and all casinos touching The Strip using normal rules. Highest score wins; if tied, most money wins; if still tied, no further tiebreak is given. A player also wins immediately upon reaching 90 or more points.
evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — End and winner

operative_quotes: 2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.

**Do not build on F block.** During setup, **discard any F-lot card and draw a replacement**; use the two accepted A–E cards for starting lots and money. Discarded F cards remain discarded.

During a turn, an **F-lot card places no marker**, but still causes the normal **owned-lot money and indicated casino money/points**. Discard it in its appropriate pile, then **repeat Draw** until an A, B, C, D or E card has been drawn and resolved. Only then proceed to Play. Thus multiple payouts can happen on one turn; you do not take actions between these draws. **End of Game still ends the game immediately** if drawn during this sequence.
answers.answer: In two-player setup, discard an F card and replace it; the two accepted starting properties must be A–E. Do not build on F block. During a turn, an F card places no marker but still triggers the normal lot and indicated casino payouts; discard it and repeat Draw until an A–E card resolves, then proceed to Play. Thus multiple payouts can occur before actions on one turn. End of Game still ends immediately if drawn during the sequence.
